input.quote: ARTICLE III OWNERSHIP Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.
input.rationale: Article III (p0048) vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights in Licensor, and "Derivative Work" (p0005) sweeps in any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements incorporating the Licensed Technology. Article VII(b) (p0087) contemplates paid customization and a "unique client front end" built for us, so the work product we commission and fund falls to Licensor with no licence back beyond the narrow, non-exclusive, Field-of-Use-limited, term-limited, non-modifiable and non-sublicensable grant in p0030/p0040-p0047 — Vendor owning deliverables with no licence back fails even the fallback (which requires a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables). There is also no statement anywhere in the agreement that we retain rights in our own data: the Confidential Information definition (p0004) runs one way in Licensor's favour, and Licensor's IP definition (p0014) expressly reaches "know-how or other data or information, software, databases". Licensor keeping ownership of the E-Path FX platform itself is acceptable, so our redline is a narrow carve-out to Article III: assignment to us of the deliverables we pay for, a perpetual royalty-free licence to any Licensor pre-existing IP embedded in them, our retained ownership of Licensee Data, and no joint ownership. The fallback licence formulation is offered in the comment if assignment is resisted.

proposal.summary: Add deliverables/Licensee Data ownership carve-out to Article III Ownership
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article III gives Licensor ownership of everything, including the customization and front-end work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b), with no licence back and no statement that our trading data remains ours. We have added a carve-out so we own the deliverables we fund (with Licensor keeping its pre-existing platform IP and granting us a perpetual, royalty-free licence to anything of its embedded in them) and retain all rights in our own data; if ownership of the deliverables is not workable, we can accept a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense them instead.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing: (i) all customization work, unique client front end, work product and other deliverables developed by Licensor specifically for Licensee and paid for by Licensee (including under Article VII(b)) (collectively, the "Deliverables") shall be the exclusive property of Licensee, and Licensor hereby irrevocably assigns to Licensee all right, title and interest (including all intellectual property rights and Moral Rights) in and to the Deliverables, excluding any Licensed Technology or other intellectual property of Licensor existing prior to or developed independently of the Deliverables that is incorporated therein, as to which Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up licence to use, modify and sublicense such incorporated materials as part of the Deliverables for Licensee's business purposes; (ii) Licensee retains all right, title and interest in and to all data, orders, trading records, client information and other information provided or generated by or on behalf of Licensee through the Licensed Technology ("Licensee Data"), and Licensor acquires no right or interest in Licensee Data other than the limited right to process it as necessary to perform its obligations under this Agreement; and (iii) nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to Licensor, or creates any joint ownership of, any intellectual property of Licensee or any Licensee Data.
